name: Regime-armed pullback-continuation: gate ON, but enter on a SHORT-term dip inside an uptrend
rationale: THESIS: Buying breakouts pays the worst fill. Inside an armed risk-on regime, the better entry is the PULLBACK — a short-term dip (negative ret over a few days) WITHIN an intact longer uptrend (positive ret over many days). The macro_regime gate is what makes the dip safe to buy: in a risk-off tape a dip keeps dipping, but in a paid-risk-premium regime a shallow pullback inside an uptrend reverts to trend. So entry combines: macro_regime>floor (gate) AND ret_Nd(long)>trend_floor (uptrend intact) AND ret_Nd(short)<dip_ceiling (currently pulling back). This is structurally distinct from breakout-momentum and gets cheaper fills (lower turnover, buy weakness not strength). DISCONFIRMER: run the SAME regime gate + long-uptrend condition but enter on raw POSITIVE short momentum (ret_short>0, a breakout) instead of the negative-short dip. If breakout-entry reproduces the pullback-entry net-of-fee Sharpe, the dip-buy structure adds nothing and this collapses to plain regime-gated momentum — falsified. The pullback structure must add edge (better fills / higher hit-rate) over the breakout version under the same gate.
catalyst: Inside an armed risk-on macro regime, price puts in a short-term pullback while the multi-week uptrend stays intact — a discounted continuation entry.
